heading: INT. COUNTING HOUSE - SECOND FLOOR - NIGHT

units.text: INT. COUNTING HOUSE - SECOND FLOOR - NIGHT
London, 1858.
Gaslight, brown and thick.
High desks lined with ledgers.
A tall window veiled by fog.
The smell of ink and coal.
HENRIETTA PLUMB, 40s, a bookkeeper in grey wool, sits upright at a slanted desk, her pen scratching steadily.
A pince-nez perches on her nose.
Her spine is straight as a rule.
CONSTABLE OAKES, 20s, bulky and young, stands at the door with a lantern, shifting from foot to foot.
A GENTLEMAN, 50s, sits in the visitors' chair with his hat on his knee.
Silk cravat, a watch-chain, hands that have never lifted anything heavy.
Evening, Mrs. Plumb.
units.name: OAKES

units.text: Constable.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: This gentleman says he has an appointment.
units.name: OAKES

units.text: Does he.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: I wrote.
units.name: GENTLEMAN

units.text: I received no letter.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: I'm sure it was lost in the fog.
units.name: GENTLEMAN

units.text: Everything is.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: She sets down the pen.
Squares the ledger.
Looks at him for a long time over the pince-nez.
Your name, sir?
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: Blackwood. Asher Blackwood.
units.name: GENTLEMAN

units.text: And your business?
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: Your employer owes me a sum.
units.name: BLACKWOOD

units.text: Mr. Tarrant owes many people many sums.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: Mine is larger.
units.name: BLACKWOOD

units.text: Then I would like to see your paperwork.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: Blackwood draws a folded paper from his coat and sets it on her desk.
She unfolds it with two fingers, as if it were a dead moth.
Her eyes travel down the page.
Is it genuine, ma'am?
units.name: OAKES

units.text: It is very well forged.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: I beg your pardon.
units.name: BLACKWOOD

units.text: Mr. Tarrant never signs with a loop on the T.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: Blackwood's smile does not falter, but his hand drifts toward his coat.
Oakes lifts the lantern.
The light jumps across the ledgers.
Sir, I'd keep your hands where I can see them.
units.name: OAKES

units.text: Naturally.
units.name: BLACKWOOD

units.text: He lifts both palms.
Henrietta folds the paper in thirds and slides it into a drawer.
She locks it.
Constable, you may escort Mr. Blackwood to the door.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: Yes, ma'am.
units.name: OAKES

units.text: We'll meet again, Mrs. Plumb.
units.name: BLACKWOOD

units.text: I do hope not. I have the books to close.
units.name: HENRIETTA

units.text: They go.
The door shuts.
She takes up her pen and writes the date at the top of a clean page, and the nib does not tremble once.
